summary: Each metric is converted to a 0-100 score with fixed breakpoints (piecewise-linear, not relative to other neighbourhoods). Metrics are averaged into categories using the weights below, and categories into the overall score. Distances and shares are measured from where residents live (municipal address points on residential zoning, with apartment addresses weighted by their units), weighted by population.

categories.label: Safety
categories.description: Crime near homes and serious traffic collisions.

metrics.label: Violent crime near homes
metrics.description: Police-reported violent incidents (2023-24) on residential land, plus half of those on main-street / mixed-use land, per 1,000 residents per year. Residents are the 2021 Census population grown by the homes built since. Small neighbourhoods are shrunk toward the city rate.
metrics.source: Ottawa Police Service Criminal Offences; City of Ottawa Zoning By-law 2008-250

metrics.label: Property crime near homes
metrics.description: Break-ins, theft, vehicle theft, mischief and arson on residential land, plus half of those on mixed-use land, per 1,000 residents (grown since 2021) per year, shrunk toward the city rate.
metrics.source: Ottawa Police Service Criminal Offences; City of Ottawa Zoning By-law 2008-250

metrics.label: Injury collisions on local roads
metrics.description: Injury collisions (2022 and 2024; the City has not published 2023) per 10 km of non-freeway road per year. Fatal and major-injury collisions count three times and any collision involving a pedestrian or cyclist counts double. Freeway collisions are excluded. Shrunk toward the city rate for short road networks.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Traffic Collision Data; Roads - Classification

categories.label: Schools
categories.description: Results at the schools residents would most likely attend, and how far away they are.

metrics.label: Nearest elementary schools (EQAO)
metrics.description: For each home, the 3-year EQAO average of the nearest English public (OCDSB) and English Catholic (OCSB) elementary schools, averaged across residents. EQAO results also reflect family income, not only school quality.
metrics.source: Ontario School Information and Student Demographics (2022-23 to 2024-25); City of Ottawa Schools

metrics.label: Nearest high schools (EQAO / OSSLT)
metrics.description: For each home, the 3-year average of Grade 9 math and Grade 10 literacy results at the nearest OCDSB and OCSB secondary schools.
metrics.source: Ontario School Information and Student Demographics (2022-23 to 2024-25)

metrics.label: Distance to an elementary school
metrics.description: Average straight-line distance from homes to the nearest public elementary school of any board.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Schools

categories.label: Amenities
categories.description: Share of residents who can reach everyday destinations nearby.

metrics.label: Grocery store within 1 km
metrics.description: Share of residents living within 1 km (straight line) of a grocery store.
metrics.source: Ottawa Public Health food premises, categorized

metrics.label: Park within 400 m
metrics.description: Share of residents within 400 m of the edge of a City park.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Parks and Greenspace

metrics.label: 5+ places to eat within 800 m
metrics.description: Share of residents with at least five restaurants, cafes, bakeries or pubs within 800 m.
metrics.source: Ottawa Public Health food premises, categorized

metrics.label: Recreation facility within 1.5 km
metrics.description: Share of residents within 1.5 km of a City pool, arena, rink or community centre.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa recreation facilities

metrics.label: Distance to a library
metrics.description: Average distance from homes to the nearest Ottawa Public Library branch.
metrics.source: Ottawa Public Library

categories.label: Getting Around
categories.description: Frequent transit, protected bike routes, and how far homes are from downtown jobs and highways.

metrics.label: Peak transit service near home
metrics.description: Weekday 7-9 am departures per hour within 400 m (bus) or 800 m (O-Train), counting each route and direction once, averaged across residents.
metrics.source: OC Transpo GTFS

metrics.label: Distance to downtown
metrics.description: Average straight-line distance from homes to downtown (Parliament Hill), the city's largest employment centre.
metrics.source: Computed from resident locations

metrics.label: Protected bike route within 400 m
metrics.description: Share of residents within 400 m of a multi-use path, cycle track or segregated bike lane. Painted lanes, suggested routes and paved shoulders don't count.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Cycling Network

metrics.label: Distance to a highway
metrics.description: Average distance from homes to the nearest freeway or provincial highway.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Roads - Classification

categories.label: Nature
categories.description: Tree cover, nearby large greenspace, and parkland per resident.

metrics.label: Tree canopy
metrics.description: Share of land under tree canopy (2024). Ottawa's urban forest target is 40%.
metrics.source: ONS-SQO / City of Ottawa tree canopy 2024

metrics.label: Large greenspace within 1 km
metrics.description: Share of residents within 1 km of a park or nature area of 4 ha or more (City or federal/NCC land), or an NCC Greenbelt trail.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Parks and Greenspace; OpenStreetMap (for NCC and provincial land); NCC Greenbelt trails

metrics.label: Parkland nearby per 1,000 residents
metrics.description: Hectares of City parkland within 1 km of each home divided by the residents who share it. The City's planning standard is 2 ha per 1,000 residents.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Parks and Greenspace

categories.label: Affordability
categories.description: Typical rent and home value, from one consistent source for every neighbourhood.

metrics.label: Typical rent
metrics.description: 2021 Census median monthly rent, adjusted for the share of tenants in subsidized housing (which pulls a census median below what someone moving in would pay), then scaled to today's market by one citywide factor (median ratio of sourced 2024-25 listings to 2021 Census rents).
metrics.source: Statistics Canada 2021 Census via ONS-SQO; Zumper / CMHC / RentCafe listings for the citywide factor

metrics.label: Typical home value
metrics.description: 2021 Census median value of owned dwellings, scaled to today's market by one citywide factor (median ratio of sourced recent sales to 2021 Census values).
metrics.source: Statistics Canada 2021 Census via ONS-SQO; AgentInOttawa / Zolo sales for the citywide factor

categories.label: Health & Environment
categories.description: Emergency care, primary care, overdose burden and traffic noise.

metrics.label: Distance to an emergency department
metrics.description: Average distance from homes to the nearest 24/7 adult emergency department (Civic, General, Queensway-Carleton, Montfort). Hospitals without an emergency department (Riverside, Royal Ottawa, Bruyère, Saint-Vincent, the Rehabilitation Centre) don't count.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Hospitals

metrics.label: Overdose ED visits
metrics.description: Overdose emergency visits per 100,000 residents per year (2020-24), shrunk toward the city rate for small neighbourhoods.
metrics.source: Ottawa Public Health

metrics.label: Homes next to major roads
metrics.description: Share of homes (apartment addresses weighted by their units) within 150 m of a freeway or 50 m of an arterial road, a standard proxy for traffic noise and air pollution exposure.
metrics.source: City of Ottawa Municipal Address Points; Roads - Classification

metrics.label: Distance to a family / walk-in clinic
metrics.description: Interim measure: average distance to the nearest family practice or walk-in clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap. OSM coverage is incomplete; this will be replaced by neighbourhood primary-care attachment rates when they are published.
metrics.source: OpenStreetMap contributors

context.label: All police-reported incidents
context.description: Every incident in the neighbourhood divided by residents. Inflated in areas with many visitors, so it is shown but not scored.

context.label: Residents used for crime rates
context.description: 2021 Census population grown by the dwellings added since (municipal address points), estimated for the crime data period, so fast-growing suburbs are not divided by an out-of-date population.

context.label: Incidents in commercial / institutional areas
context.description: Incidents on land zoned commercial, industrial, institutional or park. Reflects visitor activity more than risk at home.

context.label: Schools inside the boundary
context.description: Count of schools located inside the neighbourhood polygon. Not scored, since children often attend schools just outside it.

context.label: Walk Score (official)
context.description: Population-weighted mean Walk Score published by ONS-SQO. Shown for reference; the Amenities metrics above measure the same thing directly.

context.label: Bike Score (official)
context.description: Population-weighted mean Bike Score published by ONS-SQO.

context.label: Workers commuting 60+ min
context.description: 2021 Census. Collected during the pandemic, so shown for context only.

context.label: Average pavement age
context.description: Length-weighted average age of road surface. Age is not condition, so it is not scored.

context.label: Food inspection average
context.description: Average Ottawa Public Health inspection score. Nearly every neighbourhood is between 97 and 100, so it is not scored.

context.label: Recent listing rent (sample)
context.description: Hand-collected listing average where a source exists; marked estimate otherwise.

context.label: Recent sale price (sample)
context.description: Hand-collected sales figure where a source exists; marked estimate otherwise.

context.label: Neighbourhood Equity Index (2019)
context.description: City of Ottawa equity index used to prioritize investment. It measures disadvantage, not liveability, so it is not scored.

context.label: 311 requests
context.description: Reflects how often residents call 311 as much as conditions on the ground.
